survey: A black cast-iron cauldron sits on a stone-tile floor, seen at three-quarter view from slightly above. A thick rolled rim runs round the mouth and holds a surface of bubbling green liquid. The round, bellied body sits on short cylindrical legs with flared feet. One leg is at front left and one at back right; a third leg of a tripod could plausibly be hidden behind the body. Every visible foot rests flat on the floor and casts a contact shadow. There is one handle on each side. The left handle is a loop hung from a lug just under the rim. The right handle is a ring hung from a square block on the side of the body, lower than the left one. A small fire of crossed sticks burns on the floor under the base, in the gap between the legs. The body is clear of the flame, so the fire could heat it.

errors.what: The two handles should be a mirrored pair but do not match. The left one is a loop attached just under the rim. The right one is a ring on a square block set lower down the side of the body, and its lug and loop are a different shape and size. A cast cauldron has two identical handles at the same height.

fix: Give the cauldron two identical handles placed symmetrically on opposite sides at the same height just below the rim. Each should be a matching iron ring hanging from a matching small lug cast into the body.
